student_text: Variable lookup in Python searches the Local scope first, then Enclosing functions, Global module, and Built-ins.

student_text: A closure occurs when an inner function remembers and accesses bindings from its enclosing function after the outer has returned.
reference_answer: A closure is a function object that retains access to variables in its enclosing lexical scope even after that scope has finished execution. Default parameter values are evaluated once when the function is defined; using mutable objects (like lists or dicts) retains mutations across subsequent calls, leading to shared state bugs. The standard fix is using None as default.

student_text: Raise explicitly instantiates and triggers an exception, halting normal execution and propagating the error up the stack.
reference_answer: All built-in exceptions inherit from BaseException, while standard application exceptions inherit from Exception. Chaining with "raise NewException from err" explicitly preserves the original causal context on the __cause__ attribute. Catching BaseException or using bare except captures SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt, preventing graceful program shutdown.
